- Family reunification
Non-EU nationals in Italy holding an EC long-term residence permit or a residence permit of  at least one-year  duration can seek family reunification.
In addition, with the exception of holders of an EU Blue Card or an Intra-company residence permit, the non-EU national must have legally resided in Italy for at least 2 years before they can apply for family reunification.
This procedure allows you to bring your immediate family members to Italy to maintain family unity.
Eligible family members include spouses, minor children (of legal age only if unable to provide for essential needs due to health issues), economically dependent parents under the age of 65 or parents above the age of 65 provided that they have no other children in the country of origin.
This orientation guide was prepared with the assistance of the Global Mobility team of the Italian law firm LEXIA, which specializes in Immigration, Labour and Tax Law.
- REQUIREMENTS FOR FAMILY REUNIFICATION
- REQUIRED DOCUMENTS FOR THE APPLICATION
- I HAVE SUBMITTED THE REQUEST. WHAT’S NEXT?
REQUIREMENTS FOR FAMILY REUNIFICATION
To obtain entry clearance (nulla osta),  it is necessary for the non-EU citizen already legally residing in Italy to submit the application  for reunification at the Immigration Desk of the Prefecture ( Sportello Unico per l’Immigrazione ), using the dedicated computerized procedure available on the Ministry of the Interior's  website .
From the date of the nulla osta request, it takes up to  180 days  for the issuance.
Once the nulla osta for family reunification is issued by the Immigration Desk, the family members for whom the nulla osta was requested can apply for an entry visa to Italy at the competent Italian diplomatic-consular authority of the country of origin. On that occasion, they must submit the  certification proving the family relationship.
The documents need to be  translated and legalized (or apostilled) .
REQUIRED DOCUMENTS FOR THE APPLICATION
- A copy of the residence permit held by the applicant. The total duration of the residence permit must be at least one year. The request can also be submitted if you hold an expired permit and the receipt of its renewal application;
- A €16.00 revenue stamp duty . The stamp number must be entered in the designated fields on the electronic forms. The original revenue stamp must be presented at the time of the appointment at the Immigration Desk “(Sportello Unico per l’Immigrazione”);
- Copy of passport (data page) both for the entry clearance applicant (already residing in Italy) and family members abroad;
- Healthcare insurance ( only for a request for family reunification of a parent over 65 years old );
- Photocopy of the lease agreement (with receipt of its registration with the Italian Revenue Agency); or photocopy of purchase deed (with registration number);
- Certificate of house suitability (“idoneità abitativa”), issued by the Municipality for family reunification purposes ( link );
- A declaration of hospitality in favour of the family member signed by the applicant for the entry clearance (the family member already legally staying in Italy). A declaration written by the owner(s) of the apartment on the S2 form , confirming consent to host the reunited family members as well;
- Official documentation (duly apostilled or legalized) confirming the family relationship : family status, birth certificate, marriage certificate (they can be requested).
Additional documents for employees :
- Latest tax return or employer’s certification of income (“ certificazione unica ”)
- Photocopy of the employment contract
- Notification of Employment to the social security body ( Unilav )
- Latest payslips
- Self-declaration from the employer, drafted on the S3 form , indicating the current employment relationship (two copies of each document)
- Copy of employer's ID
Additional documents for self-employed professionals :
Freelance professionals :
- Copy of Registration with the professional order or VAT Number attribution
- Submission receipt of Modello Unico
Sole proprietorship ( Ditta Individuale ) :
- Certificate of registration with the Chamber of Commerce
- Copy of VAT number attribution
- Tax Return (Modello Unico) and submission receipt
Additional documents for owners of a Company:
- Recent company’s certificate issued by the chamber of commerce (“ visura camerale ”)
- Tax Return ( Modello Unico ) and submission receipt
- Copy of ID of all owners
If the documentation submitted is deemed complete and suitable, the user will be able to download the Nulla Osta from the Ministry of the Interior's  website .
Citizens residing in Milano who wish to request information, guidance, and support regarding the family reunification procedure can contact "RaggiungiMI" at the "WEMI Inclusione" Service Center of the Municipality of Milano at wemi.raggiungimi@comune.milano.it
Users are encouraged to check their applications through their SPID credentials.

I HAVE SUBMITTED THE REQUEST. WHAT’S NEXT?
Once the Nulla Osta has been obtained, the family member to be reunited must go to the Italian Consulate in their home country to apply for a family reunification visa for Italy.
Within 8 days of entry in Italy by the family member, they must then notify the Immigration Desk (“ Sportello Unico per l’Immigrazione ”) at the competent Prefecture of their arrival and wait for the appointment.
At the appointment, the original documentation supporting the application will be verified and the family member will receive the residence permit application form to be submitted to the Police headquarters via post office.
Note : For the family reunification procedure, we recommend contacting a law firm to support you in the procedure.
